title: Yathirajaswamy Betta
tagline: Bengaluru → Bidadi → Ramanagara → Yathirajaswamy Betta. ~58 km, a bare granite hillock with a cave shrine and old fort remains.
summary: Yathirajaswamy Betta, also called Kote Betta, is a bare granite hillock near Thimmasandra village, about 8 km north of Ramanagara off the Ramanagara–Magadi road. Bikes are parked in a mango orchard at the base, and rock-cut steps lead up in about 20–30 minutes to a small cave temple of Yathiraja (Ramanujacharya) beside a perennial spring, with traces of an old fort on top. From the summit you get a 360-degree view over Ramanagara's boulder hills.

segments.note: Fast run out of the city on the expressway or its service road.
Past Bidadi to the Ramanagara traffic signal; turn right towards Magadi.
~8 km towards Magadi, left towards Koonumuddanahalli, hill on the right after ~1 km.

highlights: Short climb on rock-cut steps to a whitewashed cave shrine
Remains of an old fort on the summit

offroad.summary: Paved all the way; the hill itself is climbed on foot, not ridden.
notes: Bikes park at the base in a mango orchard
A Google Maps interior route via Dharapura skips Ramanagara town on village roads

timings: Open all day; no entry hours
~20–30 min climb up, about an hour in total on the hill
Early morning is best, before the rock heats up
cautions: Steep, near-vertical faces near the summit; stay on the steps
Temple is often locked with no priest present
No shops at the base; carry water
Litter from picnics around the base; carry yours back
